# Applying the scale on each platform

The principle is the same everywhere: **one place applies the scale** (the
design system's text components, or one helper they call), and every screen
uses those components. Screens never set font sizes, and never switch scaling
off.

## React Native / Expo

React Native follows the system setting by default (`allowFontScaling` is
true). It can cap growth (`maxFontSizeMultiplier`), but it can't set a floor.
So the kit applies the whole range itself:

```tsx
// src/theme/textScale.ts: generated by scale-table.mjs --emit ts
// src/components/ui/Text.tsx
import { Text as RNText, useWindowDimensions } from 'react-native';
import { scaledText, TextRole } from '../../theme/textScale';

export function Text({ role = 'body', style, ...rest }: { role?: TextRole } & TextProps) {
  useWindowDimensions();                 // re-renders when the user changes their text size
  return <RNText allowFontScaling={false} style={[scaledText(role), style]} {...rest} />;
}
```

- `allowFontScaling={false}` is right **here only**: the component applies the user's setting itself, within the range. Anywhere else it is a bug, and `text-scale-audit.mjs` reports it.
- `TextInput` needs the same treatment: same helper, same component.
- `useWindowDimensions()` makes the component re-render when the setting changes while the app is open. `PixelRatio.getFontScale()` then returns the new value.

Icons need the same: the generated file has `scaledIcon()` and `ICON_SIZES`.
An icon set with a plain number (`<LogOut size={18} />`) stays 18 while the
text beside it doubles. The kit's `Icon` sizes every icon from the scale, and
screens use it:

```tsx
// src/components/ui/Icon.tsx
export function Icon({ as: Glyph, size = 'md', ...rest }) {
  useWindowDimensions();
  return <Glyph size={scaledIcon(ICON_SIZES[size])} {...rest} />;
}
```

## iOS (SwiftUI and UIKit)

Use text styles, which follow Dynamic Type, and limit the range per view:

```swift
Text("Today's plan").font(.body)                          // follows Dynamic Type
Text("Welcome").font(.custom("Brand-Bold", size: 34, relativeTo: .largeTitle))
VStack { … }.dynamicTypeSize(.xSmall ... .accessibility2)  // the range for this screen
```

UIKit: `UIFontMetrics(forTextStyle: .body).scaledFont(for: font, maximumPointSize: 34)`
and `label.adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`. Set a floor by choosing the
base font so that the smallest category still lands above it.

## Android (Compose and Views)

Text sizes in `sp` follow the font scale; `dp` and `px` ignore it. Android 14
and later already scale large text less than small text, so headings grow more
gently on their own.

```kotlin
// Compose: hold the scale within the policy for a subtree
val density = LocalDensity.current
val held = density.fontScale.coerceIn(0.8f, 2.0f)
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalDensity provides Density(density.density, held)) { content() }
```

For a per-role cap, compute the size from the role's base and `fontScale`, as
the React Native helper does.

## Flutter

```dart
MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(minScaleFactor: 0.8, maxScaleFactor: 2.0, child: app)
```

Never `textScaler: TextScaler.noScaling`. Per-role caps: wrap large display
text in its own `MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(maxScaleFactor: 1.25, …)`.

## Web

The browser's text-size setting changes the root `rem`; page zoom scales
everything. Size text in `rem`, never `px`, and never fix the root size in px.
The generated CSS holds each role between a floor and a ceiling:

```css
/* generated by scale-table.mjs --emit css */
:root { --text-body: clamp(14px, 0.9375rem, 30px); }
p { font-size: var(--text-body); }
```

**Import the generated file.** `--emit css > src/theme/text-scale.css` only
writes it; nothing loads it until the entry CSS does:

```css
/* index.css */
@import './theme/text-scale.css';
```

A Tailwind config that reads the file knows the names, so classes build and
the build passes, but the browser never gets the values: every `var()` falls
back silently and icons sit at their default size. The audit reports a
generated file that nothing imports.

**Use the project's own prefix.** If the design system's tokens are `--ds-*`,
emit with `--prefix ds` (or `"cssPrefix": "ds"` in the config) to get
`--ds-text-body` and `--ds-icon-md`, one family rather than two.

Icons beside text use the generated `--icon-*` sizes, which grow with the
text up to 1.5× (or `1em`, for an icon that should match its text exactly).
A fixed size (`size={18}`, `w-[16px]`, `width="16"`) stays put while the text
doubles. Tailwind's `w-4 h-4` is rem, so it grows with the setting (without a
ceiling); the audit doesn't flag it, but the kit should still use `--icon-*`
so icons stop at 1.5×:

```css
.icon { width: var(--icon-md); height: var(--icon-md); flex-shrink: 0; }
```

Don't pass the variable as a size prop (`<LogOut size="var(--icon-md)" />`):
most icon libraries write it into the SVG's width attribute, where `var()`
doesn't work. The kit's `Icon` sets width and height with a class instead,
which overrides the attribute.

Never disable zoom (`user-scalable=no`, `maximum-scale=1`).
